text_blocks.snippet: Several medications can affect potassium levels, leading to either high (hyperkalemia) or low (hypokalemia) levels. Diuretics, especially potassium-sparing ones, and certain ACE inhibitors, can increase potassium levels. Conversely, some diuretics (like loop diuretics) and other medications can lower potassium. Certain antibiotics, NSAIDs, and immunosuppressants can also influence potassium levels.
